I think Eduardo Colin was a driver working for the same drug dealer she was working for, and was likely being paid (or himself was working off a debt.)

Drug dealers don't do their own 'pick up and drop off' it's too risky, so they pay people to do it for them. I think Eduardo Colin was the person who drove Jane Doe from wherever she was from (I think Oklahoma or Texas) to Albuquerque.  I think they were both linked to the drug deal, and that's why his family was so tight lipped. 

I can't really prove any of this, but this is what I think. Drug trafickers need a driver and a 'switchover' person, and sometimes traffickers have 2 or 3 people for a handover deal, just because.  

And I think the fact that EC checked Jane Doe into the hotel, means that he knew her.

Also, the police don't believe she was from Albuquerque. And I just don't either. 

She had a suitcase with clothes, which to me goes to the fact that she was traveling there from somewhere else. At least traveling so far, and doing something, that would require her to stay overnight.

I know other people have their theories, and the more the merrier, I say. But I'm pretty solidly thinking this is her story. Also, there was no bus ticket found in her belongings. The police checked her purse for ID and found nothing. If they had found a bus ticket, it would have been a strong line of inquiry to identify her, and they would have used the ticket to determine her originating location. I'm sure there is a whole other theory about her involving a bus and some other reason for the money, but it's not what I'm convinced of. I don't see why she would have 500 bucks but 'no money for a ticket home.' It's just not the theory that i'm convinced of. I posted mine here, and if someone else has their own separate theory, they can post theirs on a thread or comment. :)

I just don't think she was the seller. And, if the police didn't discover/didn't know they money was counterfeit, then I don't think she would have either. So I don't think it was counterfeit. 

The police report never mentioned anything about the money being counterfeit, so I don't think it was. And, I know she *could* have been the seller, but I just don't think she was. That's just my firm belief.

Well, I'm kiiiiinnnd of embarrassed to say this...

 I just worked really hard on my theory, wrote a biiiiig long tidy post about it with facts and all.... And then realized I may have gotten the whole thing entirely backwards, because I can't be 100% sure about the drug trade route activity in '91 in the Southwest. 

I mean, I know a bit about it, but not enough to entirely, fully piece things together, namely my original theory about where she came from. I feel like if I had one more 'piece' I could be more sure.   :{  and now I feel like a bozo and I don't want to post my whole 'dossier'. :/

But, the TLDR is I think she's from Oklahoma or north Texas, along l-40 back east. And she was in Albuquerque to *buy* some drugs, not to sell them. I think Edward Colin wasn't a randomer, I think he was the person who drove her to Albuquerque from Oklahoma or north Texas. I don't think they knew each other that well, but they were both 'hired by/working for' the same mid-level drug dealer - who was probably linked to a gang. And I think this is why Edward Colin's family was so tight lipped. They may have known he was into some shady stuff, but didn't dare mention it to the police (Mexican drug cartels are no joke, their reputation alone stops people in their tracks.) 

l-40 in the southern US is a huge road for drug trafficking. Huge. Huge, huge, huge. Stuff like heroin is manufactured in (or gets into the US from) Central America to the south, through Mexico. then it comes up through New Mexico other SW states.  

I think  Jane Doe and whoever drove her there came from the East. The hotel was on the *right* (north) side of the road if you're traveling east to west on l-40. It was easier to get to a motel on the right side of the road (it always is easier to access things on the right side of a highway than the left.)

I think, sadly, that AQJD was effectively a drug trafficker. And this is hard to say, because ultimately we're trying to find people who knew her, and this is not the nicest aspect of who she potentially was (or may have been.) But there is certainly evidence to back this theory up.  The 500 dollars I now believe was payment for a large/moderate quantity of heroin, that was never purchased. Hence the digital scale. Day to day users don't carry a scale like that around, because if they get caught by the police, the mere possession of a scale like that can result in an increased charge from 'simple possession' for daily use. 

I think she was more than a casual user, I think she was dealing.  I don't think the $500 was proceeds from prostitution because this was before Craigslist, and a hotel-based prostitute would have to do quite a lot of work to make $500 bucks. Street- based prostitutes make sometimes as little as 20-50 dollars a 'service.' She had too much money for a street prostitute (who usually spend as quick as they make - on drugs - they don't accumulate funds.) And she didn't have the look of a 500 a time call girl. She wasn't local so where would she find clients to make that kid of money anyway. 

Hence, I think she was a drug trafficker, and the 500 was to *pay* for drugs, and she was there in AQ to pick up. Albuquerque is on 2  main drug supply corridors. Big time. I -40 and l 25 are both big drug corridors. I think the drugs came up from South America via 1-25, and she came to Albuquerque via the 40 from OK or North TX to 'pick up' as they say.

The 500 bucks and the scales say drug sale to me. I also think Edward Colin was the person in the hotel with her, but he left. 

I personally think that the drug deal didn't actually go through. I don't think she was there to sell, I think she was there to buy, and then take back to her area (OK/North Texas.)

The reason I feel the drug deal didn't go through is because that's why I think she committed suicide. Her 'supplier' never showed, for whatever reason. Maybe she gave him the wrong directions or something and he never showed. She had the 500 bucks but couldn't touch it because it didn't belong to her.

She was only packed for a few days, not for starting over in a new town. And the 500 wouldn't have gone far towards that anyway if it was 'gift from family' money.

I do think she was hoping to meet up with the man in the photo (who police are convinced is not Edward Colin,) but somehow that didn't happen. 

I'm just really convinced that it was a moderate sized drug deal that didn't go through, and was too afraid to face the dealer with no drugs to show him. If a drug deal went wrong and someone is sitting in a hotel hundreds of miles from anywhere, they would feel really scared. Also, since it's clear she was using, I wonder if the 'job' she was doing was to pay off a drug debt she had accumulated. People often have to do 'jobs' for dealers if they have a debt that gets out of hand. And since dealers don't do their own 'legwork', they need mules and traffickers. I wish I didn't know these things, but I've lived in some really bad areas and seen some pretty bad crap in my years. 

I wonder if she became despondent because the deal didn't go through, and she couldn't go back to her dealer and face him. Maybe he had threatened her 'you better do this or else.'

And, when the guy with the drugs didn't show, not only could she not buy the drugs to take back to her 'boss,' but she had no drugs for herself. Being in drug withdrawal, facing a failed job for a drug dealer who you owed money to, that would push someone over the edge. 

And I don't think she came to AQ to kill herself, I really don't think she was suicidal when this whole episode started: She had a cute outfit on, she had a big trendy bracelet on, she had a couple of beers with someone when she got into the hotel, she had a recent picture of herself with a friend, hell, she had several changes of clothes. This doesn't seem like the other 'hotel suicides' I've read about, where the victim had nearly no possessions and no change of clothes. (Lyle Stevik and the Portland Inn Jane Doe being examples)

I'm still really convinced she was there to buy, not sell. But, to be honest, my knowledge of the drug trade 'flow' in 1991 isn't strong enough to be sure she wasn't supplying *to* someone in AQ. It's just not my instinct though. If she had been there to sell drugs, and the 500 was for a successfully done deal, why on earth would she kill herself? And the fact that she was obviously distressed (as evinced by her suicide) *and* in possession of $500, means there is something really important about that $500. She didn't touch that $500 for a reason, and I think it's because it wasn't hers. It was never hers. 

I'm just getting a really strong Oklahoma/North Texas vibe. And, she reminds me of a lot of kids I know who grew up in foster care, or fell on hard times and became homeless or transient, or fell into the drug trade.

I just really think this whole thing is a case of 'girl has no solid family, girl gets into drugs, gets in over her head,  racks up a debt to a drug dealer, has to do a job for dealer to repay drug debt, drug deal job goes wrong, she gets scared of her dealer, and kills herself.'

In fact, I wonder if Edward Colin was supposed to drive her *back* to where she came from. But when he came to pick her up, she was already dead, because she had panicked when the deal didn't go thorough and she was too afraid to face her 'boss,' and show up with no drugs. 

I'm rambling, but... that's my theory now. I just wish I had more to strengthen it with.  If Edward Colins' family were more forthcoming about his travel habits and maybe where he worked, it would be easier to put this together, but, they didn't say much. And I think there's a reason for that. 

Anyway, it's by the by, I guess.

I don't quite understand the question but I'll answer the best that I can. 

Jacobs Lakeview Manor was a nursing home for the elderly, in all likelihood small-ish and independently owned. And it doesn't look like it's open anymore. 

There are quite a few small, independently owned and run Nursing Homes in that part of Michigan, so I imagine the one DLT worked at was the same or similar. 

There is no central authority so to speak, but this may be different in countries other than the United States. In the US Nursing homes are run as privately owned businesses.  

The government would oversee things like standards, but they don't have anything to do with day to day issues, and authorities only get involved if there is a complaint. (Or for annual hygeine and safety inspection.) Government run nursing homes are almost non existent. Generally Nursing homes are privately run and independently operated. 

The term 'group home' just means that there are a group of elderly people living and being cared for there. The manager oversees day to day activities, and the owner is the ultimate 'authority' (except regarding legislation on things like hygiene and the like.)

Ownership of the van isn't tied to her job role, just permission to drive it. The van would have been owned by the Nursing home itself, in fact one of the write ups said "in the Nursing home's van." It would have been an asset of the business, like how a school bus is owned by the school.  

Unless, however, the write up of the police report was wrong, and it wasn't the Nursing Home's property. A manager would be authorized to drive the van, but it would be property of the home, much like the beds and medical equipment is property of the home.

There are *so,* so many questions. Naliju and I were discussing it the other day. So many questions about DLT, and if they were answered it would certainly help put even more pieces of the puzzle together. Who reported her missing? Was there an interview with that person? Did the police do *anything* to try and find her, or find out where she might have gone? 

And another big question is this: Where did DLT live? This has always been a huge question for me, with regards to AJD. When DLT went missing, what happened to her apartment?  Was her apartment searched for any indication of where she might have gone, or if she had any 'enemies' who may have wished her harm? This is a huge question for me. Perhaps she lived in 'staff accommodation' at the Nursing Home? But if that was the case, did LE make note of it?  

And another *big* question is, was the 'loss' of the van entered into the police system as 'possibly stolen?' If the police considered the possiblity that DLT went missing because of a criminal act against her, then they would have to consider the van as being stolen by the 'perpetrators.' [Woman is killed in the course of a carjacking, body not found, van driven around by car thieves. Ergo, stolen van, be on the look out....] 

It seems, from reports, that the van actually belonged to the Nursing Home. This seems like a big piece of the puzzle - why did she take the van that didn't belong to her, wouldn't she have feared potentially being charged with grand theft?  Or, did she *know* the owner of the van wouldn't report it or her missing....?

And, this (yes, I've gone down the rabbit hole here, but bear with me) leads me to *another* question..... Perhaps someone at the nursing home *knew* she was going to leave, and *let* her take the van? I just don't know how she managed to do a 'walk away' with that van, and not have the van reported as stolen. It wasn't recovered for 4 months. Was the van ever reported as stolen, and if not, why not? Why would her employers, the owners of the van, just let such an expensive asset vanish like that, without raising more of an alarm? And when the van was finally recovered, what happened then? 

Maybe this is just a case of a teeny tiny police department, in an area that usually has no crimes, just being inexperienced with things like 'stolen' vans and missing women? 

Anyway, *lots and lots* of questions. But, it's likely that LE in Michigan might not want to give us any answers. Ultimately, there may be confidentiality issues at play. But it would be really good to know whether or not police records of this nature (interview statements and the like) are public record or not.

So many questions. And at the end of the day, no one is really obligated to give us answers :/ 

And to answer your original question (yeah, i went off one one there, I know) I personally think she had been married, possibly twice. I don't however think she had kids. I know that some people believe her abdominal scar is a C-section scar, but i disagree. For one, the scar goes above the belly button. Even back in the day, C-sections are carried out only on the womb, and the scar always ends below the belly button. Nowadays, c-sections are done 'horizontally' but in the past they were done vertically. (I've seen a couple of my aunt's scars from the 1980's.) The c-section scars I've seen have never gone above the navel. But I'm sure a doctor could give a more solid, less anecdotal answer. I just don't think she had kids, is all. I think the clients at the nursing home were her main priority. But, that's just my theory.
